PRIORITY (USER, s495, 2026-09-22): LOW.  "If stage 0 is cheap, please put that in the todo list", then: "Ah, do give stage 0 a low priority."  It sits with #2097 (one-liner switches) at the bottom of the queue: only when nothing above it waits; never ahead of an everyday-number batch.

DESIGN: docs/scope-exit-destroy-design.md section 4 (Stage 0).  Probe: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/destroy/d1.pl (perl's ten timing shapes; after this task PCL prints all eleven `DESTROY` lines, the ten early ones LATE -- at exit -- and row 10 in perl's place).
BUILD: (1) `bless` into a class for which method resolution finds a NON-EMPTY `DESTROY` (an empty body -- the AUTOLOAD-guard idiom, 16 of core's 46 -- registers nothing) pushes a WEAK pointer to the referent on a registry; the per-class answer is cached beside the method cache and invalidated with it (a `sub DESTROY` defined later, `@ISA` changed, a re-bless into another class = re-decide).  Classes without DESTROY pay one cached flag test per `bless` -- MEASURE it on the OO bench rows (moo-objs, methret, the bless-heavy ones), FLAG > 1 %.  (2) At exit, AFTER the END blocks (perl's order; probe `END { print "end\n" }` with a live object), every registered object still alive and not yet destroyed gets `DESTROY`, newest first, each in its own handler: a die inside DESTROY is warned `(in cleanup) ...` on stderr and never changes the exit status; `$@ $! $?` are saved and restored around each call (perl localizes them -- File::Temp's DESTROY relies on it) and the exit status the program chose survives (#2009 is the neighbour: END's `$?`).  (3) A per-object `destroyed` mark so nothing is destroyed twice by the registry; an EXPLICIT `$obj->DESTROY` does not set it (perl calls it again at exit too -- probe).  (4) `exit` inside DESTROY, `die` at top level (objects are still destroyed), `POSIX::_exit` (skips everything), `exec` (perl does NOT destroy), a forked child that exits (it destroys ITS copy -- File::Temp guards on `$$` for exactly that: probe that the temp file survives the child).
PROBE THE BREAKING CASES: an object resurrected by its own DESTROY (stores `$self` in a global -- call once, never again); DESTROY that creates new objects of a DESTROY class during global destruction (perl destroys them too; do not loop forever -- drain until empty, with a bound); 100k objects of a DESTROY class (the registry must not make `bless` or the GC quadratic: a weak vector compacted when it doubles, not a list scanned per bless); objects already collected (the weak pointer is dead: skip).  Order between objects at global destruction is UNSPECIFIED in perl -- do not write a guard row that asserts an order perl does not promise.
NOT IN SCOPE: DESTROY at scope exit (Stage 2 = #2370, PARKED by the USER), filehandle close at scope exit (Stage 1 = #2006(b)).
BAR: `cl/` runtime => full sweep + the op/ companion leg (`op/ref.t`, `op/bless.t`, `op/die_exit.t`, `op/universal.t`); the acceptance rows named in not-supported.md's DESTROY section (ref.t 63-64, grep.t 69-76, bless.t's lifetime rows) are RE-MEASURED -- some need scope-exit timing and stay failing: say which; `tools/everyday-smoke.pl` before -> after (`idioms/destroy-scope` stays DIFF -- it asserts scope timing -- but `modules/File-Temp` may move once #2056 is fixed); guard rows in a Pl/t OO file, inverse-verified; docs/not-supported.md's DESTROY section REWRITTEN (the residue: "DESTROY runs at program exit, not at the last reference"); docs/ir-spec.md gets the rule; README's DESTROY bullet is the USER's -- propose the sentence in the report.

=== USER RULING (s538, 2026-11-11; paraphrased) ===
Asked what scope-exit DESTROY would cost (build time and run time), the USER heard the design doc's numbers and ruled: build Stage 0 (this task) now; Stage 2 (#2370) is decided later, with the point-4 write-up of the s538 compatibility plan and its board numbers.  The README and the other documents are updated in the same batch (the README DESTROY bullet is no longer "propose only": the batch edits it, the reviewing session reads it).  Brief s538/s538b-prompt.md adds three measurements the documents depend on: A what "still alive at exit" leaves out (objects the collector reclaimed earlier get no DESTROY -- the registry stays WEAK; a bounded alternative is a proposal, not built), B the cost of bless, C exit time for 100k objects.


=== DONE (s538b, 2026-11-13, Opus; resumed in s539 and s540) ===
BUILT (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only, runtime-only, no generation): the gate `*p-destroy-live*` (opened in %p-note-sub-install by a NON-EMPTY sub named DESTROY or AUTOLOAD; the p-sub macro marks an empty body), ONE weak vector filled by p-bless while the gate is open, %p-destroy-pin at the exit hook's first step, %p-run-global-destruction after the END blocks and before the flushes (newest first, each once, class + destructor read at exit, AUTOLOAD fallback with $AUTOLOAD, empty skipped, void context, a perl die silent, exit ends the phase with its status, objects blessed during a round drained up to 100 rounds, ${^GLOBAL_PHASE} = DESTRUCT).  NOT the brief's per-class cache at bless: deciding at exit makes a re-bless, an @ISA change and a late DESTROY right with nothing to invalidate.  NOT the brief's $@/$!/$? save/restore: perl 5.40.3 localizes none of them at global destruction (probed), and a DESTROY's $? IS the exit status.  ir-spec Â§7.4a; guard Pl/t/destroy-exit-01.t (30 rows; inverse on 53dd73da: 23 fail).
MEASURED: A the s495 probe 11 of 11 calls (10 late, at exit), 3 of 11 with a forced full GC as the last statement; 100,000 made-and-dropped objects -> 9,727 calls at exit (perl 100,000 at scope exit), 0 with the forced GC; a File::Temp object dropped in a block -> file removed at exit; a guard in a returned sub -> released at exit, lost with the forced GC (SBCL keeps no dead variable's value).  B no measurable cost on a program with no destructor (blessnew 1M blesses: tree 0.393/0.395 s vs base 0.412/0.409 s, two quiet passes, inside methret's noise band); with a destructor in the program ~22-35 ns per bless (blessdes +5.4..5.6 %, blessnew-d +7.4..8.5 %) -- FLAGGED, kept (USER s536).  C 100,000 live objects destroyed in 0.052 s at exit (perl 0.016-0.018 s), load 1.4.
ROWS: sweep ref.t "DESTROY called on array elem" / "on closure variable" pass (204 -> 206, TOTAL 18,798); companion op/ref.t 210/32 -> 215/30, op/bless.t 111/6 -> 112/6 (rows DESTROY subs print now print, at exit); board Try-Tiny context.t 25/0 (all rows, rc 255: Test::More's END counts before the finally blocks run), finally.t 23/7 all 30 rows (17 18 23 = #4866), IO-Compress 104destroy-* / Path-Tiny sig_die.t temp.t unchanged (scope timing, #2370); everyday 116 -> 116, destroy-scope still DIFF line 1 (order now after/destroyed).
BARS: gate 370 / 12,077 PASS; sweep GATE clean 0 new / 0 LOST, drops 5; corpus-diff vs 53dd73da IDENTICAL; ir-conform 328 / 0 / 17 / 0; EVERYDAY 116 of 122 (--record 61404e80).
